case.presentation: A 50-year-old man with IgA nephropathy, diabetes insipidus, and recurrent UTIs presents with suspected drug allergy after Bactrim for UTI: pruritus and hives on arms/trunk began after the 4th dose; patient self-discontinued after the following dose. He also noted dark urine, and labs showed AKI (Cr 2.5 from baseline 1.2) that resolved over the next month. He previously tolerated once-daily low-dose Bactrim for 6 months 10 years ago. Does the patient need sulfa allergy testing? Is the AKI part of an allergic reaction or a separate adverse effect?
case.recommendations: Recommend continued avoidance of Bactrim and sulfa antibiotics. End-organ damage as demonstrated by his AKI is a contraindication to allergy testing and reexposure. The timing (rash after a few days) is more consistent with a delayed-type adverse reaction rather than an immediate IgE-mediated reaction; thus, skin testing (for immediate reactions) is not helpful. If no acceptable alternatives exist and a sulfa antibiotic is required, consult Allergy & Immunology for further discussion and counseling. Consider routine referral to Nephrology in a few months given his underlying IgA nephropathy and recent AKI.
